title: The 52-Hertz Whale: The Loneliest Voice in the Ocean
narration: A whale sings at fifty-two hertz. Blue whales hum at ten-forty. Fin whales groan at around twenty hertz. This one? Alone at fifty-two, a lone voice in a vast, indifferent ocean where most whales never even hear its call.
visual_goal: A lone whale surfaces in deep blue ocean, its breath misting in the cold air. A soundwave visualization pulses at 52Hz, glowing faintly against the dark water. Sudden cut to a spectrogram with a single, glowing 52Hz spike standing stark against a silent ocean of black and blue frequencies.

title: A Call No One Answers
narration: Since nineteen eighty-nine, this whale has sung every year. thirty-five years of calls. No matching replies detected. Just the endless, echoing silence of the deep.
visual_goal: A year counter ticks from 1989 to 2024, each year flashing with a spectrogram of the 52Hz call. No answering calls ever appear—only empty space where replies should be.

title: Why 52 Hertz?
narration: Blue whales can't hear it. Its frequency is outside the typical range for fin whales as well. A pulse in the static, too high, too strange for any known whale song.
visual_goal: Split screen: a blue whale’s call (10-40Hz) fades into static, while the 52Hz spike remains, pulsing like a heartbeat in the dark. The blue whale’s call flickers and dies, leaving only the lonely frequency.

title: The SOSUS Secret
narration: The U.S.. Navy's SOSUS array picked up its call, initially for military purposes but later used for scientific analysis. A signal no one expected to intercept.
visual_goal: A black screen with green sonar blips flickering like distant stars. A single 52Hz blip appears, labeled 'SOSUS'. The screen dissolves into grainy, declassified Navy footage of hydrophone arrays being deployed in the 1960s.

title: 3,000 Kilometers of Silence
narration: Its call travels three thousand kilometers across the Pacific. Yet no matching replies have been detected. Too high. Too strange. Or is the ocean simply too vast for any reply to reach?
visual_goal: A map of the Pacific Ocean stretches across the screen. A red line traces 3,000km from the whale’s position near California, fading into the abyss. No other whale calls appear along the route—only empty blue silence.

title: The AUVs Listen
narration: Autonomous underwater vehicles now glide through the deep, their hydrophones listening. They detect the fifty-two hertz call. Still alone. Unanswered. Singing into the void.
visual_goal: A sleek AUV glides through the dark ocean, its red lights cutting through the black water. A hydrophone icon appears, detecting the 52Hz call in real-time. No other calls are detected—only the lonely frequency.

title: Every Month, Every Year
narration: January to December. nineteen ninety-four to two thousand twenty-four. Always fifty-two hertz. Always alone. A rhythm of solitude that never wavers, never changes, never finds an echo.
visual_goal: A hand-drawn calendar flips through months and years. Each month flashes with a spectrogram of the 52Hz call—identical, unchanging. No variation, no reply, just the same lonely song.

title: Is It Really Lonely?
narration: Or is it just singing in a language we don’t understand? A frequency we’ve never heard before, a voice from a world we’ve barely begun to explore.
visual_goal: The whale swims in deep blue, its body outlined in bioluminescent trails. A soundwave visualization of the 52Hz call ripples outward. The scene fades to abstract ocean waves, swirling like ink in water.

title: The Mystery Remains
narration: We’ve tracked it for decades. We’ve mapped its path. We’ve listened to its song. Yet we still don’t know: who is it? A blue whale with a rare mutation? A hybrid? Something entirely unknown?
visual_goal: A spectrogram of the 52Hz call fills the screen, the spike glowing like a beacon. A question mark overlays it, pulsing faintly. The screen fades to black as the mystery lingers.

title: The Loneliest Voice
narration: In the ocean’s endless noise, one voice sings at fifty-two hertz. And no one answers. Not in nineteen eighty-nine. Not in two thousand twenty-four. Not ever.
visual_goal: The whale dives into the deep blue, its silhouette shrinking into the abyss. The soundwave visualization of the 52Hz call fades into silence. The screen fades to black with the title, leaving only the echo of a song no one hears.
